issues.legal_issue: An appeal does not abate when the claim concerns the entire subject matter, the surviving parties represent that subject matter, and the opposing parties knowingly allow the appeal to proceed without raising abatement.
material_facts: A public group sought to establish a customary burial right over the entire suit property, and the trial decree applied to the whole property and all defendants.
One defendant appealed the whole decree. During that appeal, another defendant died and his legal representatives were not substituted.
The plaintiff-respondents knew of the death but raised no objection to abatement, and the appeal was decided on its merits.
The plaintiff-respondents later raised abatement in a further appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appeal had not abated, and the plaintiff-respondents could not raise the abatement objection for the first time in the further appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Where parties proceed on the basis that a deceased party is represented by the surviving parties, and the claim survives against the subject matter as a whole, a party that knowingly allows the appeal to proceed on the merits without objecting to abatement cannot later reopen the matter on that ground. The Court applied Dondapani Sahu v. Arjuna Panda, [1969] 3 SCC 397.

rule.if: appeal_from_decree and deceased_party_not_substituted and common_claim_survives_against_entire_subject_matter and surviving_parties_represent_entire_subject_matter and respondents_knew_of_death and respondents_allowed_merits_hearing_without_objection

predicates.appeal_from_decree: A party appealed a decree concerning a claim against the subject matter.
predicates.deceased_party_not_substituted: A party to the appeal died, and that party's legal representatives were not substituted.
predicates.common_claim_survives_against_entire_sub: The claim asserted against the subject matter as a whole survived despite the party's death.
predicates.surviving_parties_represent_entire_subje: The surviving parties to the appeal represented the subject matter as a whole.
predicates.respondents_knew_of_death: The opposing parties knew that the party had died during the appeal.
predicates.respondents_allowed_merits_hearing_witho: The opposing parties allowed the appeal to be heard and decided on its merits without objecting to abatement.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a claim that survives against the entire subject matter, the surviving parties represent that subject matter, and informed opposing parties allow a merits hearing without objection, the appeal does not abate.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should use its power to modify a decree for all affected parties when a common, indivisible claim concerns the entire subject matter and limiting relief to the sole appellant would leave inconsistent results.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed a customary right over the entire suit property, and the trial decree applied generally to the property and all defendants rather than identifying particular portions for particular defendants.
The sole appellant challenged the whole decree, while the alleged right could not be exercised only over a particular piece of the property.
The High Court held that the customary right was not established but set aside the decree only as against the appellant, leaving it in force against other defendants.
The resulting decree would have rejected the claimed right as to part of the property while allowing the trial decree based on the same right to remain in force as to the rest.
issues.conclusion: The High Court ought to have exercised its appellate power to modify the decree for all affected parties; the Supreme Court modified the decision and dismissed the suit in respect of the entire property.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives an appellate court broad discretionary power to pass the decree that ought to have been passed, including in favour of parties who did not appeal or cross-object, to do complete justice and avoid contradictory decisions. The power should be exercised with care and caution, but in an appropriate case it should be used. The Court relied on Mahabir Prasad v. Jage Ram, [1971] 1 SCC 265; Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh, [1975] 1 SCC 212; Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal, [1969] 3 SCR 944; and Koksingh v. Smt. Deokabai, [1976] 1 SCC 383.

rule.if: appeal_from_common_decree and sole_appellant_challenged_entire_decree and claim_asserted_over_entire_subject_matter and claim_not_capable_of_partial_exercise and appellate_finding_rejected_common_claim and decree_left_in_force_against_nonappealing_parties and result_is_inconsistent_across_subject_matter

predicates.appeal_from_common_decree: A party appealed a decree that resolved a claim common to multiple parties.
predicates.sole_appellant_challenged_entire_decree: The only appellant challenged the decree as a whole.
predicates.claim_asserted_over_entire_subject_matte: The claim was asserted over the subject matter as a whole.
predicates.claim_not_capable_of_partial_exercise: The claimed right could not be exercised only over a selected portion of the subject matter.
predicates.appellate_finding_rejected_common_claim: The appellate court found that the common claim was not established.
predicates.decree_left_in_force_against_nonappealin: The appellate court left the decree in force against parties who had not appealed.
predicates.result_is_inconsistent_across_subject_ma: The resulting decisions treated the same claim inconsistently across the subject matter.
predicates.appellate_court_should_modify_decree_for: The appellate court should modify the decree for all parties affected by the common claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a common decree, the claim covers the entire subject matter and cannot be exercised partially, and limiting relief would leave inconsistent results, the appellate court should modify the decree for all affected parties.
